task: Add `parse_username(value)` to app/users.py. It takes a string, strips surrounding whitespace and returns it. A valid username is 3 to 20 characters of lowercase ASCII letters, digits and underscores, and starts with a letter. Reject anything else with `ValidationError`.
why:
Both are equal on scope, fidelity and correctness, so maintainability decided it, and here that came down to the tests.
c1's tests cover the "lowercase" rule with an uppercase input ("Ada"). They also check that a newline inside the name is rejected, which a `$`-anchored regex would let through. And they check that a non-ASCII digit is rejected.
c2 (runner-up) never tests an uppercase username, even though "lowercase" is a core part of the request. A later change to a case-insensitive check would still pass its tests.
